title: Mario Party 7
subtitle: A cruise with room for eight
summary: Mario Party 7 is Hudson Soft's final GameCube entry in the series, released in North America on 7 November 2005.
body: Mario Party 7 is Hudson Soft's final GameCube entry in the series, released in North America on 7 November 2005. Toadsworth hosts a cruise through six themed boards, each offering a different way to compete for Stars. The game also expands some modes and minigames to eight people. Its party grows through pairs sharing resources and decisions, adding another layer of cooperation to a format normally driven by individual turns. A teammate becomes someone to consult before the next dice roll or item choice.

The boards attach different rules to earning Stars. Pagoda Peak changes their price as players reach the summit, Pyramid Park encourages stealing with Chain Chomps, and Windmillville ties Stars to ownership of windmills. These differences make the destination more than a new background for the same purchase. The player must first understand what resources or positions matter there. Coins earned in minigames can become the means of claiming an investment, buying an opportunity or taking a prize directly from another competitor.

In team modes, partners move together and share coins, Stars and Orbs, alternating responsibility for choosing routes and items. The minigames can split the gathering into several configurations, including challenges built for eight participants. Microphone activities return alongside ordinary controller games. Hironobu Yahata and Shinya Outouge again composed the music. The cruise brings the GameCube run to a close by increasing both the size of the gathering and the variety of board rules, making agreement within a team as useful as winning against the others.
